reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) shows Ag addition in a TiNbZr alloy reduces friction and increases strength, but it does not support the key premises that Ag microalloying and annealing in CoCrFeMnNi will induce grain-boundary segregation, nor that the mechanism involves a pre-formed Ag network acting as a lubricant across the wide temperature range; the cited mechanism is tribologically-induced nanocrystal formation, not annealing-driven segregation.
premises: Ag addition to a multi-component alloy can form a self-lubricating nanostructure during wear
Ag segregation or precipitation can reduce friction coefficient
Ag addition increases alloy strength via solid solution strengthening
The proposed Ag microalloying and annealing will induce surface segregation of Ag along grain boundaries
The Ag-rich network will act as a solid lubricant across a wide temperature range (-50°C to 500°C)
